claim: The new wrapper silently drops every diagnostic whose location is not in source, including Location.None. This affects types declared in the compiling assembly, not only metadata symbols. Example: `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` returns null whenever the declaring syntax is not a PropertyDeclarationSyntax, such as a positional record property declared by a ParameterSyntax. So BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull for an in-source `record R([property: Key((string)null)] int X)` is now discarded instead of reported. The source defect then goes unflagged, although the requirement only asks to stop crashing for symbols with no declaring syntax.

claim: The new `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` filter drops every diagnostic whose location is null, and `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` returns null for any source property not declared by a `PropertyDeclarationSyntax`. claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops every diagnostic whose Location is not IsInSource. Diagnostics created with a null location (Diagnostic.Create(..., (Location?)null, ...) gives Location.None) are now silently suppressed. Several existing diagnostic paths use helpers that can return null (GetIdentifierLocation, GetLocation(parameter), GetParameterListLocation). For source types whose syntax is unavailable or located elsewhere, the diagnostic previously reported with no location and now disappears. This changes diagnostics in users' builds (e.g. MsgPack003/004/005/etc.), and an error-level diagnostic being lost can turn a failing build into a passing one.
